heroDescription: Use the Hitelecom H100-HTC1800 dome-camera reference as a starting point for industrial-site visual monitoring. Develop the configuration around the scene, observation distance, lighting, installation conditions and receiving system. Agree the optics, imaging, power and connection requirements, then validate the proposed configuration against representative site conditions.
reviewNotice: H100-HTC1800 is a supplied camera design reference. Imaging and electrical specifications, supported functions and qualification evidence are established in the approved project documents.

interfaceCards.title: Start with the observation task
interfaceCards.text: Define what the operator needs to see, the target distance, scene width and relevant movement. Match image detail, coverage and lighting requirements to that task before choosing the imaging configuration.
examples: Agreed image-detail and motion acceptance criteria

interfaceCards.title: Coordinate the physical location
interfaceCards.text: Review the mounting surface, viewing direction, service access and environmental exposure. Specify the camera assembly, cable entry, installation hardware and power arrangement for the approved location.

interfaceCards.title: Define where images are used
interfaceCards.text: Identify the receiving equipment and whether the project requires live viewing, image transfer, recording or a combination. Agree the supported interfaces and application workflow in the configuration proposal.

features.title: Observation-led specification
features.text: Start with a visible target and an operational question. Define the image evidence an operator needs to understand the equipment or site activity, then turn it into measurable project requirements.

features.title: Coverage and mounting review
features.text: Coordinate the scene width, working distance, viewing angle and mounting position. Review obstructions and service access before approving the proposed optical and mechanical arrangement.

features.title: Lighting and contrast assessment
features.text: Provide representative scene images and lighting conditions, including glare, shadows and relevant low-light periods. Use them to define and evaluate the required imaging behaviour.

features.title: Image detail and motion requirements
features.text: Specify the target detail, movement and useful update behaviour for the observation task. Agree resolution, lens, exposure and frame-rate requirements as part of the camera configuration.

features.title: Power and connection planning
features.text: Define the supply, electrical interfaces and connection method for the installation and receiving equipment. Confirm cable routing, associated device loads and the approved wiring documentation.

features.title: Viewing and recording workflow
features.text: Describe who uses the images and whether viewing, transfer or recording is required. Match the camera configuration to the selected receiving system and define retention and access requirements.

features.title: Environment and enclosure review
features.text: Review the installation temperature, moisture, dust, cleaning conditions and mechanical exposure. Establish the required enclosure and supporting verification for the final camera assembly.

features.title: Documented customization and delivery
features.text: Agree the camera configuration, product identification, any associated software scope and acceptance criteria before design approval. Record the delivered version and its supporting installation and test documents.

workflow.title: Describe the scene
workflow.text: Share the observation target, scene dimensions, distance, mounting position and representative lighting. Explain what an operator must be able to confirm from the image.

workflow.title: Agree the configuration
workflow.text: Review optics, imaging behaviour, power, connection method and receiving equipment. Put the approved hardware, software scope and verification criteria into the project specification.

workflow.title: Evaluate a representative setup
workflow.text: Assess the agreed sample or configuration with realistic lighting, movement and receiver conditions. Review usable detail, coverage, integration and installation behaviour before release.

workflow.title: Document the delivered assembly
workflow.text: Hand over the configuration record, installation instructions and agreed test evidence. Identify the receiving system, operating responsibilities and maintenance access for the completed installation.

platformBullets: Image use: agree the required viewing or recording workflow, receiving equipment and available connection. Define the output method and supported functions in the configuration proposal.

faqs.a: H100-HTC1800 is a dome-camera reference for custom industrial-site visual monitoring projects. The project specification establishes the supplied imaging configuration, electrical details, connection method and supported functions.

faqs.q: Does the model name identify a resolution or viewing angle?
faqs.a: No resolution, field of view or image-sensor specification is defined by the model name on this page. Agree those parameters against the observation task and record them in the approved configuration documents.

faqs.q: How should the lens and coverage be selected?
faqs.a: Provide the target distance, scene width, mounting height, viewing direction and the detail an operator must see. Review obstructions and representative scenes, then evaluate the agreed lens and camera configuration at the intended position.

faqs.q: How are resolution and frame rate specified?
faqs.a: Start with the required image detail and movement in the scene. Agree resolution, frame-rate behaviour, exposure and the receiving-system requirements together. Evaluate useful image detail under the relevant conditions rather than selecting only by a headline pixel count.

faqs.q: Are low-light, infrared or automatic day/night functions included?
faqs.a: Define the lighting conditions and any required operating periods in the project brief. The configuration proposal identifies the imaging functions and any associated illumination included in the supply. The illustrated housing alone does not specify these functions or their performance.

faqs.q: Which power supply and connection method does it use?
faqs.a: The supplied visual does not establish a rated supply, electrical connector or communications interface. Specify the available site power, receiver and connection requirements, then obtain the approved electrical values, wiring schedule and interface definition for the selected configuration.

faqs.q: Can it work with a recorder, existing video system or cloud platform?
faqs.a: Identify the intended receiving system and required viewing or recording workflow. Review the output method, formats, protocols, access requirements and any integration work in the proposal, then validate the agreed functions together. No particular recorder, protocol or built-in cloud service is specified by this reference alone.

faqs.q: Does it provide AI analytics or machine-vision inspection?
faqs.a: This page describes visual monitoring projects for operator review. Automated classification, identification, counting, defect detection or dimensional measurement would require a separately defined and validated development scope; they are not established functions of this camera reference.

faqs.q: Can images be reviewed alongside sensor events?
faqs.a: A project may define a workflow in which authorized staff review images together with external measurement records or events. Agree the receiving software, data interfaces, time relationship and user workflow before implementation. Camera images do not replace the independent measurement or protection system.

faqs.q: Can it be installed outdoors or in a demanding industrial location?
faqs.a: Review the complete installation against temperature, moisture, dust, cleaning, mechanical exposure and any site-specific qualification requirements. Confirm the enclosure, mounting and supporting evidence for the final assembly before selection. A dome-style appearance does not establish an ingress, impact or hazardous-area rating.

faqs.q: Are the application photographs examples of camera image quality?
faqs.a: They illustrate the observation environments and project tasks. They are not recorded H100-HTC1800 footage, installed customer examples or demonstrations of image resolution, low-light performance or analytics. Use representative sample evaluation to confirm actual imaging performance.

faqs.q: What should a camera customization enquiry include?
faqs.a: Share scene photographs, the observation target, required detail, distances, mounting position and lighting conditions. Add the available power, receiving system, connection needs, environmental requirements, expected quantity and delivery documents so the proposal can define configuration, development and acceptance scope.

enquiryIntro: Share the scene and what the image must help your team understand. Include mounting conditions, lighting, available power and the intended receiving system so we can review the H100-HTC1800 reference and define the proposed camera configuration and validation scope.
